# PART 1 – Credibility and tools {.darkslide background-color="rgba(0,0,0,0)"}

::: {.partlabel}
Part 1
:::

::: notes
Part 1 starts further back than you might expect, with what science is for, why anyone thinks it is in trouble, and the red-card study, in which twenty-nine teams analysed one dataset and reached different answers. We then take what open research proposes as the remedy, and the evidence of three very large studies, published together, which measured how often findings in the social sciences survive being repeated, with a first look at the study in which I took part. We end on the tools, because the sharing, the checking and the repeating are all made easy or impossible by software.
:::
